identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kamakshi Amman Temple is counted among the eighteen principal Shakta Pithas and is the foremost goddess shrine of Kanchipuram. Kamakshi is enshrined seated in padmasana, holding a noose, a goad, a sugarcane bow and a flower arrow. A Sri Chakra placed before the image is traditionally attributed to Adi Shankara, and the temple is the seat of the Sri Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham.

governance.establishedEra: Attributed variously to Pallava patronage (c. 5th-8th century) and to the Cholas; substantially modified between the 14th and 17th centuries
governance.managingAuthority: Sri Kamakshi Ambal Devasthanam, Sri Kanchi Kamakoti Peedam, Sri Madam Samasthanam; listed by the HR&CE Department, Government of Tamil Nadu

narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple's founding is not settled in the sources consulted: it is attributed to Pallava kings of roughly the fifth to eighth centuries, while some accounts credit the Cholas with its construction. It was substantially modified between the fourteenth and seventeenth centuries.

The temple is counted among the eighteen main Shakta Pithas and is the seat of the Sri Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham, the monastic institution that is closely bound to its ritual life; the HR&CE listing itself names the temple as the Devasthanam of that Peedam. Adi Shankara is honoured with a shrine in the complex and is credited with consecrating the Sri Chakra yantra placed before the principal image.

The inner Gayatri Mandapam is described in temple tradition as having four walls standing for the four Vedas and twenty-four pillars for the twenty-four syllables of the Gayatri mantra. The Bila gate marks the point where, by tradition, the goddess emerged to defeat the demon Bhandasura.

visitingInfo.officialContactNote: The HR&CE page's published hours for this temple are internally garbled, so timings should be confirmed directly with the Devasthanam on 044-27222609 before travelling.

openingHours.notes: HR&CE lists a morning session of 5:30 AM to 12:30 PM, consistent with the Ko Pooja at 5:30 AM. The same page also mentions early access from 3:45 AM, which is not otherwise explained.

The HR&CE page prints the afternoon/evening session as 3:45 PM to 9:00 AM, which is evidently a typographical error; 9:00 PM is recorded here, consistent with the Ardhajama pooja ending at 8:40 PM. Not treated as settled.

poojas.description: The last pooja of the day.

festivals.processionOrRituals: Street processions of the deity, including the chariot festival.

shrines.locationDescription: The central sanctum, where the goddess is seated in padmasana on a throne, holding a noose, a goad, a sugarcane bow and a flower arrow.
A Sri Yantra installed before the principal image, traditionally credited to Adi Shankara.
The inner hall enclosing the sanctum; its four walls are traditionally identified with the four Vedas and its twenty-four pillars with the twenty-four syllables of the Gayatri mantra.
A shrine in the complex honouring the philosopher, whose Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham is seated at this temple.
The temple has four entrance gopurams.
